The pre-phase-3 HARDENING sweep (B2+B3 over the whole phase-1/2 route band) came back structurally clean — scope-pins, token lifecycle, rate buckets, twins all verified — with three fix-nows, shipped here before phase 3 sends anonymous crawler traffic at these surfaces:

This is the masterplan's own §6 rule (minors never indexed; athlete pages public only for adult+public profiles): a manager's entry must never put a private athlete's full name on a crawlable, CDN-cached page. ### [`v0.12.1`](https://redirect.github.com/Cldfire/nvml-wrapper/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0121-released-2026-03-27)

- Corrected `NVML_FI_PWR_SMOOTHING_*` field IDs which used CUDA 13.0U1 numbering instead of v12, causing silent data corruption on CUDA 12 hosts ([#​134](https://redirect.github.com/Cldfire/nvml-wrapper/issues/134), [#​137](https://redirect.github.com/Cldfire/nvml-wrapper/issues/137))

- Fixed `nvmlDeviceGetActiveVgpus` argument ordering ([#​128](https://redirect.github.com/Cldfire/nvml-wrapper/issues/128))

- `FieldIdScheme` enum and `Nvml::field_id_scheme()` to inspect the detected driver's field ID numbering
- Method for getting vGPU type ID ([#​124](https://redirect.github.com/Cldfire/nvml-wrapper/issues/124))

items.title: fix(core): prevent metadata from shadowing page_content in format_document

labels.name: fix
labels.description: For PRs that implement a fix

items.body:
Fixes #40075.

## Problem

`_get_document_info` builds the template variables dict as:

```python
base_info = {"page_content": doc.page_content, **doc.metadata}
```

Because the metadata spread comes *after* the `page_content` key, any metadata
field named `page_content` silently overwrites the document's real content. The
formatted output then contains the metadata value instead of the actual text,
with no error or warning.

This is a silent data corruption: the caller gets a confidently wrong result, and
nothing in the chain signals that the document's content was replaced.

## Fix

Swap the spread order so the explicit key always wins:

```python
base_info = {**doc.metadata, "page_content": doc.page_content}
```

This is the same pattern used in the Bedrock fix (#40022) for an analogous issue.
Metadata fields other than `page_content` are still available as template
variables; only the shadowing is prevented.

## Tests

Three tests in `test_format_document.py`:

- `test_metadata_page_content_key_does_not_override_real_content` — the
  regression case: a document with `metadata={"page_content": "impostor"}`
  formats using the real `page_content`, not the metadata value
- `test_get_document_info_preserves_page_content_over_metadata` — directly
  asserts `_get_document_info` returns the real content
- `test_format_document_normal_metadata` — non-shadowing metadata still works

Verified red-first: the regression test fails with
`AssertionError: assert 'metadata impostor' == 'real document text'`
on the unfixed code.

items.title: ingestion: detect document structure and split composite PDFs before extraction
items.body:
A supplier packet — one scanned PDF holding a cover listing plus 17
separate facturas, one per page — reached the single-invoice extractor
whole and came back as one invoice with one number and one total. The
other sixteen invoices disappeared into its line items. That is silent
financial data corruption, not an extraction-quality problem: a hard
failure would have been recoverable.

Ingestion now answers "what is this document?" before it asks "what are
this invoice's fields?" (ADR-035). For every PDF batch item the worker
runs a structure stage before extraction:

- single    → extract the file as it is (unchanged path, and a multi-page
              single invoice stays one invoice)
- composite → one new batch item per document, each queued for
              extraction; the source item is discarded, its file kept
- unclear   → the item fails with extract.err.structureUnclear instead of
              being extracted as one invoice

Detection is hybrid and cheapest-first: a PDF with a text layer on every
page is segmented deterministically from that text (document number,
página N de M, cover keywords); a scan goes through the provider seam for
a page map of roles only — no invoice fields — metered as
'document-structure'. Bounds: 40 pages, 15 MB, and a provisional 0.7
confidence floor below which a composite answer is downgraded to unclear.

Segment keys are derived from the source key (ns/x_ab12cd.pdf →
ns/x_ab12cd_p2.pdf), so a redelivered job recognises the children it has
already created. Segments inherit source/sourceRef, so a WhatsApp packet
still replies once per invoice, and a document the worker never extracted
releases the monthly slot it claimed.

Verified against the reported 18-page packet: cover dropped, 17
single-page invoice documents queued, each split page byte-identical in
content to the original.
